paras: The assault on Cole near Dardanelle was an attack on a Black man named Cole by a crowd of armed and masked men near Dardanelle, Arkansas, on a Wednesday night in May 1882, probably 17 May. Cole was badly cut about the face and head, pulled the mask from one attacker he said he recognized, and took out warrants against the men.

Cole, described as "colored," lived about seven or eight miles below the town of Dardanelle. On a Wednesday night a crowd of armed and masked men assaulted him and left him "very badly used up, having cuts all over his face and head." The report gives no reason for the attack, does not say where it took place, and does not name the attackers or give their number or race.

During the struggle Cole snatched the mask off one of the men, whom he said he recognized. He then took out warrants against his assailants. No report of arrests, a hearing, or a trial appears in the coverage.

The attack is known from a single paragraph that the Memphis Daily Appeal printed on 19 May 1882 in its "Arkansas News" column, credited to a Dardanelle paper, the Arkansawyer. The item was a plain news note without headline or comment, and it ran directly before a Dardanelle magistrate's remarks on the decline of whisky cases since the town's saloons closed. The same column carried a Corning item on a mob that whipped a man suspected of burglary, to which the Corning editor added that "mob law is worse." The Appeal's text garbles Cole's given name, and no other paper's account of the attack was found.
